classification.difficultyReason: Development: connect approximate rainfall readings and actual ratios to the misleading displayed bar heights. This links routine calculations with the taught explanation of truncated bar-chart baselines.

content.prompt: This graph shows the average rainfall in three capital cities. Shelly says: “London’s rainfall is around twice that of Berlin, and four times that of Canberra”. Explain why she is incorrect.

spec.description: Average rainfall. Rainfall in mm 500,510,520,530,540,550,560,570 with break below500. Categories Berlin/Germany, London/England, Canberra/Australia. Red bars reach approximately528,568,510.
spec.answerVisibility: question; assessed misleading features intentionally retained

answer.short: The truncated axis exaggerates the bar heights. London has about 1.08 times Berlin’s rainfall and 1.11 times Canberra’s.
answer.worked:
Reading approximately, London has 568 mm, Berlin 528 mm and Canberra 510 mm.
$568\div528\approx1.08$ and $568\div510\approx1.11$.
The bars start near 500 mm, so their displayed heights do not show the ratios of the actual rainfall.
